raw / staging / analysis schemas. staging.poi is the normalized contract that src/loci/score consumes — no city-specific columns downstream of staging.

Description:
registry.yaml mirrors CONTEXT.md §3. `loci check-sources` asserts schema validity, budget ceiling, and that every dataset_id in the registry appears in CONTEXT.md — so the human and machine registries cannot drift.

It caught a real drift on its first run (MTA ridership wujg-7c2s was in the registry, missing from the charter).

Title: Drop PostGIS for DuckDB; remove Docker from the critical path
Description:
Reversed the original PostGIS choice. The only available image ran emulated (amd64 on arm64) and the 'service path' rationale was speculative.

DuckDB verified end to end: spatial + community h3 extensions, RTREE indexes, ST_Read, read_parquet, and every DDL feature the schema needs. H3 cells stringify to 15 chars, so the CHAR(15) design carried over unchanged.

No container, no daemon, no emulation penalty.

DONE — see CHECKPOINT decision D9.

Title: Obtain Census API key
Description:
Free and instant: https://api.census.gov/data/key_signup.html
Set CENSUS_API_KEY in .env. Blocks ACS ingest (E1).

Title: Obtain Google Places key with a hard call budget
Description:
Pro SKU $32/1k, 5,000 free calls/month. Budget 5,000 calls ≈ $0–100.

GUARDRAIL: request ONLY id/name/location/types. Adding ratings or hours reprices to Enterprise ($35/1k); reviews or photos to Enterprise+Atmosphere ($40/1k). Enforce LOCI_GOOGLE_CALL_BUDGET in the client.

Needed W4, not W1.

DONE 2026-09-02 — src/loci/validation/google_places.py: persisted call ledger, refuses when LOCI_GOOGLE_CALL_BUDGET is unset or exhausted, minimal field mask (id/location/types). `loci validate --dry-run` plans the spend; `--run` executes under the cap. Webmap per-click calls capped by GOOGLE_CLICK_BUDGET (default OFF).

Title: VERIFY: LODES8 block vintage is 2020 TIGER across all years
Description:
CONTEXT.md open question #5. If LODES8 uses 2020 blocks for every vintage, the 2002–2023 panel needs no 2010/2020 crosswalk. If it does not, budget a crosswalk before E3.

This is the cheapest possible check and it de-risks the entire panel. Do it first.

Source: https://lehd.ces.census.gov/data/lodes/LODES8/

Title: VERIFY: DCWP Legally Operating Businesses freshness
Description:
CONTEXT.md open question #6. The portal has shown a stale refresh date (data as of 2023). Confirm the current vintage via the Socrata metadata endpoint.

If stale: downgrade DCWP to snapshot-only and lean harder on DOHMH as the anchor.

Title: Overture Places adapter → staging.poi
Description:
GeoParquet via overturemaps-py, NYC bbox. Map Overture categories onto the 15 Loci categories (CONTEXT.md §2.1).

Overture's schema is coarse for personal services — expect the salon/laundromat mapping to be the lossy part, and record mapping confidence in staging.poi.confidence.

Title: Foursquare OS Places adapter
Description:
Apache-2.0, separate taxonomy from Overture. Used as a cross-check, not as the base layer — FSQ skews toward venues with check-in history, i.e. away from laundromats.

Why it matters under the gap screen: it is the only free bulk source with fine-grained gym / hardware / urgent-care labels — the top gap types with no government anchor.

BLOCKED 2026-09-02 on access: public S3 bucket retired (holds LICENSE/NOTICE only); data is on the Places Portal (Iceberg token) or the gated Hugging Face mirror. Adapter written (sources/universal/foursquare_places.py, tests pass); set HF_TOKEN after accepting the terms, then `loci ingest --source foursquare_os_places --dry-run` and tighten LEAF_CATEGORY against the reported unmapped leaves.

DONE 2026-09-02 — token obtained, NYC extract cached (821k rows, <1 min), category map rebuilt from the real 1,279-label taxonomy (path-prefix rules for the restaurant/bar/cafe families; Deli, ATM, Doctor's Office and specialist physicians deliberately dropped). FRESHNESS GATE added: corroboration by other sources is <10% for rows last refreshed before 2019 vs 55% for 2026, so only rows refreshed since 2024 load (109k of 191k mapped; 54k canonical). Effect on the gap screen was modest once ghosts were removed: hardware 270→245, fitness 154→138, clinic 148→91.

Title: OSM Overpass adapter
Description:
Tag vocabulary of record (CONTEXT.md §2.1 table). Also the third opinion on presence.

Carries the project's most dangerous bias — see E4 coverage validation.

Title: DOHMH restaurant inspections adapter (ANCHOR source)
Description:
Dataset 43nn-pn8j. ~30k establishments, near-census of food service — every food establishment is inspected, so within the food tier the true count is effectively known.

This is the calibration anchor for the whole coverage-bias mitigation (CONTEXT.md §7.1). Treat it as the project's most valuable data asset.

Title: DCWP licenses adapter
Description: Dataset w7w3-xahh. Laundries and other DCWP-licensed categories. Has issuance dates — the raw material for the deferred E5 license panel.

Title: NYS DOS Appearance Enhancement adapter
Description:
Dataset y3u4-jbgh. Best available source for nail/hair.

CONSTRAINT: active-only, therefore survivorship-biased. Snapshot enrichment ONLY. Must never be used to construct an openings/closings series — enforce this in the adapter, not just in docs.

Title: USDA SNAP retailer adapter (ANCHOR for grocery/convenience)
Description:
USDA SNAP Retailer Locator via its ArcGIS feature service. Near-census of stores that accept SNAP; store type separates Supermarket/Grocery from Convenience by stocking breadth.

Why: tier 1 is 40% of the index and had no anchor. Its bias runs the OPPOSITE way from OSM (misses non-SNAP stores in affluent areas), which makes it a second calibration curve for the coverage-bias check.

Verified 2026-09-02: 8,052 five-borough rows, lat/lon on every row.

Title: NYS SLA liquor license adapter (ANCHOR for bars)
Description:
Dataset 9s3h-dpkz. Anchor for the bar category, which the DOHMH adapter deliberately does not emit.

Mapping is conservative — license descriptions do not say bar. Emits `bar` for Food & Beverage Business, Club, Cabaret, Bottle Club; skips Restaurant (DOHMH) and Additional Bar riders. QUESTIONS.md H-D9 tracks the open mapping question.

Companion inactive file 6dg3-2z7i makes closures recoverable — a candidate E5 panel.

Verified 2026-09-02: 24,711 NYC rows, 98.5% georeferenced.

Title: Cross-source POI dedup / entity resolution
Description:
The same laundromat appears in Overture, FSQ, OSM and DCWP. Without dedup the DNCI inflates wherever coverage overlaps — which is itself geographically biased, so the error is not random.

Approach: spatial blocking (~25m) + normalized-name similarity, per category. Emit a survivorship record so counts are auditable.

Title: Build H3 res-9 shoreline-clipped grid
Description: ~7,400 cells over NYC's ~778 km². Drop water-only hexes; retain partial hexes with land_fraction for edge normalization (threat §7.7).

Title: PLUTO loader + commercial zoning capacity control
Description:
MapPLUTO 26v2. Extract ZoneDist1, CommFAR, ResidFAR, BuiltFAR, UnitsRes, YearBuilt; area-weight onto hexes.

REQUIRED CONTROL, not optional. Without commercial zoning capacity in the supply model the underserved tail fills with park edges, industrial zones and cemetery blocks, and the top-20 list is indefensible on first inspection.

Also supplies the dasymetric ancillary surface and the development-headroom term.

Title: MTA transit access control
Description:
Stations 39hk-dx4f, Entrances & Exits 68hr-j2j7, Hourly Ridership wujg-7c2s.

Use ENTRANCES, not station centroids — a station can be 400m of walking from its own far entrance. Ridership captures transit quality: a 12-route complex is not a single-route stop.

Caveat to record: ridership window is 2020–2024, so 2020–21 levels are pandemic-depressed.

Title: ACS ingest + dasymetric interpolation onto hexes
Description:
ACS 5-yr tract → H3 via tobler, dasymetric with PLUTO UnitsRes as the ancillary surface. Plain areal weighting would spread population evenly across parks, rail yards and cemeteries.

Propagate MOEs — do not silently treat tract point estimates as exact (threat §7.8).

Title: Staten Island leverage check
Description: CONTEXT.md open question #3. Low-density and car-oriented; may act as high-leverage points in the supply model. Include, but check Cook's distance and report results with and without.

Title: SHIP W1: POI density map + queryable DB
Description: Week-1 exit criterion. A crude choropleth of raw POI density per hex. Not the finding — proof the pipeline is real and the joins are right.

Title: Build OSMnx pedestrian walk graph
Description:
network_type='walk', 4.8 km/h (80 m/min).

Extend the graph BEYOND the city boundary so cross-boundary businesses are reachable where they genuinely are — otherwise every edge hex is spuriously underserved (threat §7.7).

Title: Multi-source Dijkstra access engine
Description:
THE performance-critical design decision. Do NOT compute ~7,400 isochrones.

For each of the 15 categories, run ONE multi-source Dijkstra seeded from every POI in that category at once, cut off at threshold distance. Nodes within cutoff are 'served'.

15 traversals instead of 7,400 — minutes not hours, and it makes the 5/10/15-min sweep affordable (45 traversals total).

Emits analysis.hex_access.

Title: Calibrate saturating k_c per category
Description:
s_c = 1 − exp(−n_c / k_c), calibrated so the first reachable establishment scores ≈0.55.

Essentials tighter (k≈1.25 — one grocery is nearly sufficient); food looser (one restaurant in a 10-min walk is thin, not complete). Revisit against observed count distributions. CONTEXT.md open question #2.

Title: DNCI: weighted geometric mean + unit tests
Description:
DNCI = Π (s_c + ε)^w_c, ε = 0.01.

THE METHODOLOGICAL CRUX. An arithmetic mean lets a hex with fifty restaurants and no grocery, pharmacy or laundromat score well — precisely the failure the thesis exists to detect. Only the geometric form punishes zeros.

Tests must include the adversarial case: 50 restaurants + 0 essentials must score LOW. If that test passes under an arithmetic mean, the test is wrong.

Title: Run 5/10/15-minute threshold sweep
Description: 10 min (800m) is the headline. 5 min (400m) and 15 min (1200m) as sensitivity and for comparability with the 15-minute-city literature.

Title: Persist hex↔business network distances (hex_poi_distance)
Description:
hex_access stored only counts at 5/10/15 min and discarded the Dijkstra results, so every new question (another walk time, distance to nearest, spacing, the Google coverage comparison) meant a two-minute graph recompute — and the threshold could not be swept.

Now: analysis.hex_poi_distance holds every (hex, canonical business) pair within 30 min with its network distance; hex_access is DERIVED from it in SQL so the two cannot disagree. gaps, spacing and the sweep read the table. `loci score` builds it.

DONE 2026-09-02 — 16.2M rows, ~3 min; derived hex_access matched the previous build row-for-row (229,133 rows; 461,421 / 1,880,500 / 4,235,014 pairs). Nearest-of-category per hex now answers in 60 ms.

Title: SHIP W2: the DNCI map
Description: Week-2 exit criterion and the first genuinely interesting artifact. Sequential palette. Sanity-check against local knowledge before proceeding to E3.

Title: Fit the supply model
Description:
DNCI ~ pop_density + median_hh_income + transit_access + commercial_zoning_capacity + land_fraction + borough FE.

Check prediction P1: the residual must have meaningful spread. If R² > 0.9 there is nothing left to explain and the thesis has no room to be true — report that honestly rather than tuning until it isn't.

Title: Moran's I + spatial error/lag model
Description:
MANDATORY, not optional. Compute Moran's I on residuals; if significant (it will be), re-estimate with pysal spreg and report both.

OLS standard errors on gridded urban data are wrong. Shipping a p-value without this is shipping a p-value you cannot defend.

Title: Residual extraction + opportunity score
Description:
opportunity = (−u_h)⁺ × transit_access × (ResidFAR − BuiltFAR)⁺.

Underserved AND transit-connected AND room to build. Any one of the three missing disqualifies the hex.

Title: LODES WAC annual panel loader 2002–2023
Description:
NY state WAC files, target NAICS 4451/4461/7224/7225/8121/8123/4441/6244. Block-level, 22 vintages.

Blocked on the LODES8 block-vintage verification (E1).

Title: LODES block → hex apportionment
Description:
Areal apportionment of block-level jobs onto H3 cells.

Document the proxy assumption loudly: LODES counts JOBS, not establishments. A ten-employee supermarket and a one-employee laundromat are not comparable units (threat §7.4).

Title: Quantify pre-2020 LODES allocation bias
Description:
Discovered while resolving the LODES vintage check.

LODES8 puts every year on 2020 blocks, but historical years got there by ALLOCATION, not observation: when a 2010 block splits, each job is assigned to a child block at random with probability proportional to AREA share. Census: 'the allocation is a statistical process and may not result in a distribution of jobs that exactly matches the areal distribution.'

Area-proportional is a poor assumption in NYC — a block splitting into a park half and a commercial half spreads jobs by area, putting employment in the park.

This is BIAS, not noise: the error concentrates where blocks were split, blocks split where development happened, and development is the outcome variable.

Size the exposure, test whether H3 res-9 aggregation actually absorbs it, and if not restrict the strongest claims to 2020+ observed data. CONTEXT.md threat 7.4(b).

Title: Validate LODES 2023 against establishment counts
Description:
Correlate the 2023 LODES cross-section against 2023 DOHMH/DCWP establishment counts per hex. Report the correlation.

This is what licenses the jobs→establishments proxy. Without it the whole panel rests on an unexamined assumption.

Title: Assemble outcome variables
Description:
Δlog population, Δlog households (ACS); Δlog ZORI (Zillow, ZIP→hex); permitted residential units (DOB/HPD).

ZIP→hex crosswalk by population weighting — CONTEXT.md open question #4. Label rent as the weakest of the four outcomes in the memo and mean it.

Title: Main growth regression (prediction P2)
Description:
Δy_{h,t0→t1} = β·u_{h,t0} + γ'X_{h,t0} + α_borough + ε, t0=2013 t1=2023.

P2 predicts β < 0 (more negative residual → more subsequent growth). A null or wrong-signed result is a real answer: it would mean gaps persist because they reflect durable demand suppression, not latent opportunity. Report it either way.

Title: Pre-trend test (2003→2013)
Description:
Estimate the same spec on the PRIOR decade. If u_2013 also 'predicts' 2003→2013 growth, parallel trends is broken and the causal reading is unavailable.

Report it whichever way it comes out. This is the check a serious reader will ask for first.

Title: Placebo outcome
Description: An outcome with no plausible mechanism — e.g. change in share of population aged 65+ — must return a null. If it doesn't, the specification is picking up generic neighborhood trajectory rather than the retail channel.

Title: MAUP sweep at res 8 and res 10
Description: Re-run the whole chain at two other resolutions; report coefficient stability. If conclusions flip with grid size, say so plainly (threat §7.3).

Title: Tier-weight sensitivity analysis
Description: Tier weights (0.40/0.20/0.25/0.15) are judgment, not derived. Sweep plausible alternatives and report whether the top-20 list is stable under reweighting. CONTEXT.md open question #1.

Title: Top-20 list + zoning-artifact audit
Description:
Produce the ranked list of transit-rich underserved hexes.

HARD GATE: manually inspect for park edges, industrial zones and cemetery blocks. Any present means the commercial-zoning control failed — fix the model, do not hand-remove the rows.

Also check it contains ≥3 genuine surprises. A list of only obvious places means the residual isn't doing any work.

Title: Spacing and nearest-missing distance diagnostics
Description:
QUESTIONS.md D5. Two read-only diagnostics the gap screen cannot answer on its own: (1) nearest-neighbour distance between businesses of the SAME category — how clustered each trade is and how often a business has no competitor within a walk; (2) for each gap hex, straight-line distance to the nearest business of its lead-missing category — separates marginal 10-minute gaps from real holes.

DONE 2026-09-02 — `loci spacing` (src/loci/model/spacing.py). Found and fixed on the way: DuckDB ST_Distance_Sphere reads (lat, lon) — decision D16, shared METRES_SQL in db.py.

Title: Residual convergence test
Description:
QUESTIONS.md T5 — does the gap close on its own?

Over 2002–2023, do hexes with a negative residual at t converge toward their peers by t+k (retail employment growth regressed on the lagged residual, borough FE)?

Why it matters: if the market already corrects undersupply, the opportunity is TIMING, not location — a different product and a different memo. Cheap once the LODES panel exists; pull forward if W3 has slack, otherwise it slides to Phase 5.

Title: Retail lead/lag timing test
Description:
QUESTIONS.md T6 — does retail lead or lag rooftops?

Cross-correlate annual per-hex changes in LODES retail employment with changes in population at leads and lags of 1–5 years.

Why it matters: 'retail follows rooftops' is the assumption the whole residual design rests on (D1). This is the one place it gets tested rather than asserted.

CAVEATS to state: ACS 5-year smoothing limits timing resolution to roughly half-decades; LODES counts jobs, not storefronts (M2).

Title: SHIP W3: empirical result + top-20
Description: Week-3 exit criterion.

Title: Design stratified coverage validation sample
Description:
Prediction P3 and threat §7.1 — the one that can invalidate everything.

OSM/Overture undercount small business in lower-income and immigrant neighborhoods: exactly the areas the thesis flags as underserved. If the undercount is strong there and weak in Park Slope, the 'retail gap' is a data gap wearing a costume.

Draw hexes at random within each income decile, and cross-stratify by foreign-born share (ACS) so borough / immigrant-neighborhood contrasts in the residual (QUESTIONS.md X3) can be separated from coverage bias. Fix n per stratum against the 5,000-call budget before spending anything.

DONE 2026-09-02 — src/loci/validation/sample.py: NTILE(10) on median income among populated hexes, seeded random draw per decile, like-for-like 800 m straight-line counts for Google vs Overture/OSM/anchor. Foreign-born cross-stratification NOT possible yet: hex_demographics has no foreign-born column (add to ACS ingest first). Default plan: 200 hexes × 15 categories = 3,000 calls, inside the free tier.

Title: Run Google Places ground-truth enumeration
Description:
Enumerate ground truth for the sampled hexes. Fields: id/name/location/types ONLY — anything more reprices the SKU.

Enforce the call budget in code. Populate analysis.coverage_validation.

Title: DOHMH-anchored undercount calibration
Description:
Within the food tier the true count is effectively known (DOHMH is a near-census). Measure OSM/Overture discrepancy vs DOHMH per hex, then use that curve to estimate expected undercount in the other tiers where no census exists.

This is the strongest available mitigation and it costs nothing extra.

Title: Coverage-bias chart
Description:
Undercount rate by income decile. NOT an appendix item.

If the finding survives this chart, the chart is the most persuasive artifact in the set. If it doesn't, this chart is how the project learns that honestly rather than shipping a bias as a finding.

Title: PMTiles export + MapLibre map
Description:
H3 choropleth, static hosting, no server. Layer toggle between DNCI (sequential) and residual (DIVERGING — zero is a real midpoint, not an arbitrary one).

Load the `dataviz` skill before writing chart code.

Title: Bivariate transit × residual map
Description: 3×3 bivariate palette. This is the map that states the thesis in one image: where transit-rich and underserved overlap.

Title: Per-category radar small multiples
Description: 15-spoke radar per top-20 hex. Answers 'what specifically is missing here — grocery, or salons?' Turns a score into an actionable observation.

Title: Scatter: residual@t0 vs growth t0→t1
Description: Fitted line + CI, borough-colored. The visual statement of P2.

Title: 4–6 neighborhood evidence cards
Description: Narrative + inset map per selected hex cluster. Does the mechanism look real on the ground? This is what converts a coefficient into something a reader believes.

Title: Methodology memo
Description:
The document a skeptic attacks and you defend. Must state plainly: the residual design reduces but does not eliminate endogeneity (§7.2); no instrument is used; what the pre-trend test showed.

Claiming cleaner identification than exists is the fastest way to lose an investment reader.

Title: Fresh-clone reproducibility test
Description:
Acceptance criterion C: fresh clone → `make nyc` → outputs in <30 min on a laptop. Pinned deps, documented lineage.

Also assert loci/score/ contains no NYC-specific column names — the portability guarantee from CONTEXT.md §10.

Title: SHIP W4: public artifact
Description: Week-4 exit criterion: public map + memo + evidence cards.

Title: DCWP license issue/expiry panel reconstruction
Description:
Establishment-level openings/closings from DCWP license dates — a true establishment panel rather than the LODES jobs proxy.

Deferred from W3 because it is ~2 weeks of data engineering with real survivorship handling. Only NYS DOS is unusable for this; DCWP is genuinely dated.

Title: Extract universal interface; run a second city
Description:
`loci run --city chicago` on universal sources only (Overture, FSQ, LODES, ACS, OSM, GTFS), with a coverage warning where NYC-grade local data has no analogue.

The half-day spent in E0 keeping loci/score/ city-agnostic is what makes this possible rather than a rewrite.

Title: Foot-traffic outcome
Description:
SafeGraph/Placekey-class data, $200–400 of the ~$400 unspent headroom. Shifts the outcome from 'did people move here' to 'did people start going here'. Nice-to-have; not load-bearing.

Spend the headroom on enlarging the E4 validation sample FIRST — that has higher marginal value because it defends against the threat that can kill the project.

Title: Identification strategy: quasi-experimental variation
Description:
Addresses threat §7.2 properly. Candidates: historic rezonings, or transit shocks such as the L-train shutdown, as sources of variation in retail supply plausibly exogenous to neighborhood trajectory.

Out of scope at 4 weeks. This is what a v2 would need to make a genuinely causal claim.

Title: Charter the premium-amenity axis (CONTEXT §11)
Description:
Owner add 2026-09-02: screen NYC for where a PREMIUM, destination amenity could open — padel courts and spa/wellness studios first.

Why this needs its own charter section and cannot reuse the daily-needs gap screen: the two goods behave oppositely.
 • Daily needs are convenience goods — consumed often, near-zero willingness to travel, so the geography is the 800 m walk and the screen is 'present in ≥80% of walkable peers, absent here.'
 • Premium amenities are DESTINATION goods — consumed occasionally, high ticket price, people will drive/transit 15–30 min for them (the owner's own premise). They are RARE by nature, so a prevalence-gap screen would flag almost everywhere and mean nothing.

So the method inverts to a classic trade-area / gravity site-selection model: a travel-time CATCHMENT with enough qualifying premium demand but little or no supply within that catchment, plus a feasible large-format site. Document it as CONTEXT §11 and CHECKPOINT D22. This is Axis 3, parallel to Axis 1 (Investability, invest.py) and Axis 2 (Rising, rising.py) — NOT a return to the rejected residual-growth thesis (D1).

Title: Define the premium-amenity bundle + demand-target per category
Description:
Padel and spa are the two named anchors; extend to the destination-amenity family that shares the travel-for-it behavior, each kept as its OWN category because catchment size, demand target and site needs differ: padel, spa / day-spa, med-spa, pilates / reformer, boutique fitness / boxing, climbing gym, bathhouse / sauna, golf & sports simulator.

Each category carries (a) its demand TARGET — not raw population: padel skews affluent + athletic + 25–44; med-spa skews affluent women 30–55; climbing skews younger + college-educated — and (b) a nominal catchment travel time and site footprint. These are judgment calls, stated explicitly and tunable, exactly like the daily-needs tier weights and the invest.py ECON minimums (D18). Emit the bundle as data (a PREMIUM dict mirroring ECON), not hard-coded in the scorer.

Title: Ingest premium-amenity supply + Google-validate (mandatory here)
Description:
These amenities are OUTSIDE the daily-needs 15, so they need their own supply layer. Sources: OSM (padel = leisure=pitch + sport=padel; spa = leisure=spa / shop=beauty+beauty=spa; climbing = sport=climbing; sauna = leisure=sauna), Foursquare leaves (Spa, Pilates Studio, Climbing Gym, Boxing Gym, Gym and Studio subtypes), Google Places for ground truth.

Why Google validation is load-bearing here, not optional as it is for daily needs: padel barely existed before 2022 and boutique studios open fast, so OSM/Foursquare snapshots undercount them SEVERELY and unevenly. A padel 'gap' is far more likely to be a data gap than a daily-needs gap is (threat: the §7.1 coverage bias, but worse). Validate every candidate site's catchment against Google + a manual web check before it ships. Reuse the budget-guarded validation client (src/loci/validation/).

Title: Travel-time catchment engine (drive + transit isochrones)
Description:
Replaces the 800 m walk ring with a per-amenity travel-time CATCHMENT — the load-bearing modeling choice for this axis, and the owner's core premise ('people will travel longer').

Build drive-time isochrones (car network) unioned with transit-time where the amenity is transit-oriented (a Manhattan spa is reached on foot/subway; an outer-borough padel box is reached by car with parking). Default 15 min, and because willingness-to-travel is ASSUMED not measured, sweep 10 / 15 / 20 / 30 min and report how the site ranking moves — the sensitivity IS the honesty here. Reuse the OSMnx graph machinery from E2; the drive network and isochrone reach are the new parts. Emits a catchment membership table (site/hex → reachable population + supply).

Title: Premium demand pool per catchment
Description:
Score each catchment's DEMAND — not raw homes (that is the daily-needs driver) but a premium demand pool: population weighted toward the top income deciles, the category's target age band, and college/education share (which D20 already computes and found correlated 0.72 with income). Per-category weighting from the demand TARGET defined in the bundle ticket.

Re-use hex_demographics (income, renter) + the ACS momentum module's age/education pulls (model/momentum.py). Output: qualifying-demand headcount and $ per candidate catchment, comparable across amenities.

Title: Large-format feasibility gate
Description:
The invest.py feasibility gate (D18) but re-tuned for destination formats. A padel court needs ~1,000+ m² and height (warehouse, parking deck, flex/industrial — often NOT a ground-floor retail bay); a day-spa needs mid-size retail or upper-floor; a climbing gym needs a tall shell. So the PLUTO test changes from 'any CommFAR>0 storefront' to lot size + floorplate + a zoning district that permits commercial recreation / personal-service, plus vacancy/industrial-conversion candidates.

Without this the screen recommends amenities onto lots where they physically or legally cannot go — the D3 zoning-artifact failure in a new costume. Gate each candidate site on a buildable/leasable large-format space before it can rank.

Title: Premium opportunity score + ranked site list
Description:
Combine: opportunity = qualifying demand pool in the catchment − existing supply reachable within that catchment, gated on a feasible large-format site, ranked per amenity.

Three threats to state plainly on the list, because a reader will raise them:
 • Supply undercount is worse for these new categories (padel especially) — every top site must survive Google + manual validation or it is presumed a data gap, not an opportunity.
 • Willingness-to-travel is assumed; the catchment radius is the biggest lever, so report the ranking under the 10/15/20/30-min sweep, not a single radius.
 • National-chain pipeline (Life Time, Equinox, Padel Haus, etc.) may already have a site under LOI — outside the data, flagged as manual diligence per top pick.

Produces the padel and spa shortlists the owner asked for.

Title: SHIP: 'Where could a padel court / spa go?' map layer
Description: Axis-3 deliverable, parallel to the invest/rising buy-list artifacts. A map layer (toggle per amenity) showing travel-time catchments shaded by UNMET premium demand, with feasible large-format sites pinned and each top site carrying its demand pool, nearest existing supply, and the validation result. Load the `dataviz` skill before writing chart code.

Title: Charter the maturity + projection axis (CONTEXT §12), honestly vs §0/D1
Description:
Owner add 2026-09-02, two linked questions: (1) where is each neighborhood on its MATURITY curve today, and (2) where could growth get to by 2033 — how do we project it.

This is the forward extension of Axis 2 (Rising, D19/D20/D21), and it MUST be framed to not revive the project's central rejected result. Be explicit in CONTEXT §12:
 • DEAD and staying dead (§0/D1): 'the retail gap/residual at t0 predicts subsequent residential growth' — β was wrong-signed (+0.069), pre-trends broken. This axis never uses the retail residual as a growth predictor.
 • LEGITIMATE and different: locating a neighborhood on a development S-curve from its OWN observed multi-metric history (income, college, rent, permits, jobs), then EXTRAPOLATING that trajectory. The pre-trend finding — that these places are on a development cycle — is precisely what licenses extrapolation.
 • The honesty is in the caveats: extrapolation assumes the frontier keeps diffusing and no macro shock intervenes. D21 already caught ENY rents COOLING to +1.9%/yr — trajectories bend, so the output is scenario bands, never a point forecast, and it is credible only if it passes the backtest ticket.

Retail (Loci's core product) attaches at the END as the dependent read: given a projected 2033 demand surface, today's Axis-1/Axis-3 sites can be re-scored forward. Write CONTEXT §12 + CHECKPOINT D23.

Title: Assemble the multi-decade neighborhood trajectory panel
Description:
momentum.py (D20) pulled only two points (2013 & 2023). Staging and projection need a real time series per NTA. Assemble: decennial 2000 + 2010, ACS 5-yr 2009/2013/2018/2023 (real HH income via B19025/B11001, college share B15003, tenure, age bands), LODES WAC 2002–2023 (already downloaded), Zillow ZORI/ZHVI 2000– (D21), DOB/HPD permit pipeline by year.

Deflate every dollar series to 2023 real (CPI ×1.308 for 2013→2023 per D20 — extend the factor to each vintage) or the trend is mostly inflation. Aggregate each vintage to 2020 NTA via that year's tract centroids (the momentum.py gazetteer method). Output: analysis.nta_trajectory, one row per NTA per year per metric. This is the raw material for BOTH the maturity classifier and the projection.

Title: Neighborhood maturity-stage classifier
Description:
Place each NTA on the development S-curve. THE methodological point: stage is defined by LEVEL and RATE and ACCELERATION (1st + 2nd derivative) of the panel metrics, not by level alone — that is what separates a maturity model from a static wealth map. A high-income but decelerating neighborhood is 'maturing'; high-income and still accelerating is 'rising'.

Stages: pre-frontier/dormant (low level, flat) → emerging (income accelerating, college still low, first permits — where ENY sits: +42% income but college only 9→14%, D21) → rising (income+college both climbing fast, rent + permit boom) → maturing (high level, growth decelerating — Williamsburg now) → mature/saturated (high, flat or declining — the 5 rich Manhattan NTAs in real decline, D20). Spatial adjacency to the already-risen frontier is a feature (gentrification diffuses to neighbors). Output: each NTA's stage + a 0–1 position along the curve.

Title: Frontier-diffusion map: where the edge moved, where it goes next
Description:
Half of 'where could growth get to' is spatial. Trace the observed gentrification frontier 2000→2023 — Williamsburg → Bed-Stuy → Bushwick → Crown Heights → Ocean Hill → East New York (D20 already found this path) — as a datable wave, and identify the not-yet-risen neighborhoods ADJACENT to today's rising edge as the mechanistic next steps.

This is the most communicable form of the forecast and the one most tied to an actual mechanism (diffusion to neighbors), so it anchors the more model-driven projection. Report the frontier's measured pace (blocks/decade) — that pace is what sets the 2033 reach.

Title: 2033 trajectory projection with scenario bands
Description:
Project each NTA's income / college / rent to 2033. Two complementary methods, reported together:
 • Per-metric LOGISTIC (saturating) extrapolation — logistic not linear, because a neighborhood cannot gentrify past 100% and linear extrapolation of a hot decade is the classic forecasting error.
 • Stage-transition (Markov) roll-forward — estimate P(stage→stage per decade) from the historical panel, then advance each NTA one step to 2033, giving a probabilistic stage.

Output is SCENARIO BANDS, never a point estimate: continued-diffusion / stall / reversal, motivated by the live evidence that trajectories bend (ENY rents cooled to +1.9%/yr post-2022, D21). Also produce the analogue read — for each emerging NTA, the already-matured NTA it most resembles at the same stage (ENY-2023 ≈ Bushwick-2011?) and that analogue's realized path as an interpretable forecast.

Title: Backtest the projection (fit 2000→2013, predict 2013→2023)
Description:
The load-bearing credibility check — the analogue to E3's pre-trend/placebo rigor, and the reason this axis is not astrology. Fit the classifier + projection on data through 2013 ONLY, project 2013→2023, and compare to what actually happened. If the model cannot retrodict the Bushwick/Crown Heights/ENY arc it demonstrably cannot forecast 2033, and the memo must say so.

Report out-of-sample error by stage (emerging neighborhoods are the hardest and the most important). This ticket gates whether the 2033 numbers ship as a forecast or only as a scenario illustration.

Title: Bridge to the product: forward-looking demand for Axes 1 & 3
Description:
Close the loop WITHOUT reviving D1. Take the projected 2033 demand surface (population/income/education by scenario) and re-score the Axis-1 investability gaps and Axis-3 premium sites against it, so a site that is marginal on today's demand but sits in a neighborhood projected to mature by ~2030 becomes visible as a forward bet.

Guardrail, stated in code and memo: retail is the DEPENDENT variable of the projection (projected rooftops/income drive projected demand), never the predictor of growth. The moment a retail gap is used to predict neighborhood growth, this has become the rejected thesis again.

Title: SHIP: maturity + 2033 projection artifact
Description: Axis-4 deliverable. Per-neighborhood: its position on the S-curve, its 2033 scenario cone (continued/stall/reversal), and its nearest historical analogue; plus the frontier-diffusion map showing where the edge goes next. Every projected number carries its backtest error. Load the `dataviz` skill before writing chart code.

Title: Charter the second-city feasibility screen
Description:
Owner question 2026-09-02: 'are there other cities with data rich enough to do similar work?' Charter the answer before building it, because the naive answer ('big cities have open data') screens on the wrong thing.

What NYC actually gives Loci, decomposed:
 • The POI layer — Overture, Foursquare, OSM, and the OSMnx walk graph — is ALREADY global and free. It ports to any city at ~zero cost and is NOT the constraint.
 • The three crown jewels ARE the constraint, and they are what a second city must reproduce:
   1. An UNBIASED near-census business anchor to correct OSM's undercount in low-income/immigrant areas (DOHMH restaurant inspections — CONTEXT §7.1, 'the project's best asset'). Without it the gap finding is coverage bias in a costume — the P3 threat that can invalidate everything.
   2. Parcel- or grid-level land use (MapPLUTO) — the dasymetric backbone that puts population where housing actually is, plus the commercial-zoning-capacity control that keeps the top list off park edges.
   3. Fine-grained demographics + transit QUALITY (ACS + MTA ridership, not mere station presence).

So the screen scores candidate cities on those three axes (anchor / land-use / demographics+transit), not on 'has an open-data portal.' Write this as CONTEXT §13 and CHECKPOINT D24. This milestone is research + city SELECTION; the universal-interface engineering that actually runs `loci run --city X` is the existing E5 ticket.

Title: Define the city-feasibility rubric as data (CITIES dict)
Description:
Emit the rubric as data — a CITIES dict mirroring how ECON (D18) and the E6 PREMIUM bundle externalize judgment — not hard-coded in prose. Each candidate city scored 0–3 on four axes, each axis naming the CONCRETE analog dataset (not 'they probably have zoning'):
 • anchor — an unbiased near-census business/establishment registry. 3 = all-industry geocoded register (Paris SIRENE, London Companies House); 2 = food+licenses near-census (NYC DOHMH, Chicago business licenses, UK FSA); 1 = licenses only; 0 = none, OSM is all you have.
 • land_use — parcel-level or gridded. 3 = published gridded population (NL CBS 100 m, Japan mesh, Nordic registers) which REMOVES the dasymetric step entirely; 2 = parcel cadastre + zoning (NYC PLUTO, UK OS, most US assessors); 1 = coarse zoning polygons; 0 = none.
 • demographics — 3 = finer than US tracts (UK output areas, INSEE IRIS, ABS SA1, register-based); 2 = US-tract-equivalent (ACS, StatCan DA); 1 = coarse only.
 • transit — 3 = GTFS + ridership/tap data (TfL Oyster, MTA); 2 = GTFS only; 1 = none.

The rubric is judgment stated explicitly and tunable, exactly like the tier weights. Score is min-gated, not summed: a city with a 0 anchor cannot be rescued by great transit, because the anchor is the load-bearing asset.

Title: Verify the universal layer actually runs outside NYC
Description: Per the CLAUDE.md habit 'verify before committing to a dependency': prove the universal core runs on a non-NYC bbox BEFORE designing the multi-city screen around the claim that it does. Pull a small Overture + OSM + OSMnx-walk-graph extract for one foreign bbox (a few km² of central London or Paris) and confirm: the Overture category map still resolves, the walk graph builds, and the H3 grid clips. Record which of the 15 daily-needs categories lose their anchor once DOHMH/SNAP/SLA/DCWP are gone — that gap IS the coverage warning the second city ships with (see the E5 second-city ticket). Cheap, and it de-risks the whole milestone.

Title: Candidate-city data dossiers
Description:
One dossier per shortlisted city, each naming the specific dataset behind every rubric axis so the score is auditable, not vibes. Shortlist and the anchor that earns it:
 • Paris / France — SIRENE, the national register of EVERY establishment, geocoded with NAF industry codes; INSEE census at IRIS level; open cadastre. Arguably a BETTER anchor than NYC (all industries, not just food).
 • London / UK — FSA food-hygiene ratings (food near-census) + Companies House (all companies); ONS 2021 census at output-area level (finer than US tracts); TfL + Oyster ridership; OS AddressBase / Land Registry.
 • Amsterdam / Netherlands — KvK business register + BAG building/address cadastre; and CBS publishes gridded population at 100 m, which REMOVES Loci's most error-prone step (the tract→hex dasymetric interpolation).
 • Tokyo / Japan — Economic Census of establishments by industry (near-census) + e-Stat census on 250/500 m mesh (gridded). Weakness: OSM/Overture POI coverage is thinner.
 • Chicago (and SF / LA / Seattle-King County / Boston / DC) — nearly free US ports: ACS, LODES, SNAP, FDIC come with the country. Chicago's all-industry business-LICENSE file is a stronger anchor than DOHMH's food-only census.
 • Toronto / Vancouver, Sydney / Melbourne, Singapore, Stockholm / Copenhagen / Helsinki / Berlin — register-based or fine-census societies; note footprint (Singapore is one small city-state) and anchor specifics.

The one-line finding to preserve: the gating asset is the unbiased anchor, and on that axis France (SIRENE), the Netherlands (KvK+CBS grid), the UK (FSA+Companies House) and Chicago (business licenses) are at least as good as NYC — several ALSO hand you gridded population, which the US does not.

Title: Generic near-census anchor adapter interface
Description: Generalize the NYC anchor concept (DOHMH/SNAP/SLA as near-census calibration sources, CONTEXT §7.1) into a pluggable adapter contract, so a second city's SIRENE / FSA / Companies House / municipal business-license file lands in the SAME staging.poi contract carrying the `anchor` flag the coverage-bias calibration already consumes. This is the piece that makes the whole coverage-bias mitigation portable rather than NYC-only — without it, a second city has the biased OSM/Overture layer but nothing unbiased to calibrate it against, and the P3 threat is un-mitigable there. Interface only in this milestone; the concrete per-city adapters are follow-on ingest tickets once a pilot city is chosen.

Title: Gridded-population adapter (skip dasymetric where a grid exists)
Description: For the cities that publish population on a native fine grid — NL CBS 100 m, Japan e-Stat mesh, Nordic and German (Zensus) grids — consume the grid directly into hex_demographics instead of running the tract→hex dasymetric interpolation (E1's most error-prone step, the one carrying ACS MOEs and the parks/rail-yards smearing risk). This is a genuine QUALITY UPGRADE over the NYC pipeline, not just a port: gridded input removes the largest single source of interpolation error. Build as an alternative demographics path selected by the CITIES rubric's land_use=3 flag.

Title: Pick the first pilot city + coverage-warning report
Description: Recommend ONE city to run first, with the trade stated: Chicago is the cheapest port (US federal data free, all-industry license anchor) and the fastest way to prove city-agnosticism; London or Paris is the strongest demonstration that the method travels internationally and that the anchor can be even better than NYC's. Whichever is chosen, produce the coverage-warning report the E5 second-city ticket requires: per daily-needs category, does this city have an unbiased anchor, or does that category run on OSM/Overture alone (and therefore inherit the §7.1 undercount)? The report is the honesty artifact — it says exactly where the second-city gap screen is trustworthy and where it is not.

Title: SHIP: second-city feasibility scorecard
Description: Milestone deliverable: a ranked scorecard of candidate cities across the four rubric axes (anchor / land-use / demographics / transit), each cell naming the concrete dataset and its 0–3 score, min-gated so the anchor dominates. Headline the recommended pilot and the reasoning. This is a decision artifact for the owner, not a public memo — it answers 'where do we take Loci next, and what will it cost to get the data there.' Load the `dataviz` skill before writing chart code.
